rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah was revealed in Madinah around the fourth year after the hijrah, following the Battle of Uḥud between Muslims and the still-idolatrous Quraysh of Makkah.
rows.anchor: was revealed in Madinah around the fourth year of the hijrah and after the crucial Battle of Uḥud

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its name reflects its extensive treatment of women’s rights, marriage, marital relations, and inheritance.
rows.anchor: much of the sūrah deals with women and their rights along with various conditions of marriage, marital relations, and laws of inheritance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of 4:1–36, 4:127–130, and 4:176 is legislative, as are its instructions for conduct in war and peace.
rows.anchor: Most of the first part (vv. 1–36, 127–30, 176) is legislative in nature, as is the section dealing with war and peace

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah ranks among Islam’s most important and foundational works for jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: among the most important and fundamental for Islamic jurisprudence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah discusses hypocrites and Jews who turned against Madinah’s Muslim community after Uhud, when Muslims were defeated by Quraysh.
rows.anchor: those Jews who turned against the Islamic community in Madinah after the Battle of Uḥud

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It addresses Jews who rejected both Christianity and Islam and Christians who divinized Jesus.
rows.anchor: those Jews who denied both Christianity and Islam and the Christians who divinized Jesus

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the most sensitive Christian-Muslim issues are Islam’s account of Jesus’s earthly end and the question of crucifixion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following an extended discussion of general religious questions, the sūrah closes with a legislative verse.
rows.anchor: the sūrah ends with a verse again related to legislative matters

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending appears to stress that Islamic belief and Muslim social conduct under revealed law are inseparable.
rows.anchor: the inseparable relation between Islamic religious beliefs and the social behavior of Muslims based on revealed Law
